messages:
sam: Kicking off a device sweep to find max payload ceilings per device (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100). Goal: tune max_batch_payload and max_tokens_per_batch for steady p95 and throughput.

tara: SGTM. What success criteria? p95 SLA + throughput?

sam: Target p95 <= 120ms for short (<512) requests, <= 250ms for long. Also watch tokens/sec and kernel_switch_count.

ryan: Posted the raw runs to perf-bot channel (link). Will share summaries here.

sam: Initial aggregated table (first pass):

```
A10  : max_payload=64k tokens  p95=95ms  kernel_switches=120
T4   : max_payload=48k tokens  p95=110ms kernel_switches=90
L4   : max_payload=56k tokens  p95=88ms  kernel_switches=70
A100 : max_payload=120k tokens p95=75ms  kernel_switches=300
H100 : OOM at 200k, stable at 160k p95=60ms
```

leila: The A100 kernel_switches spike suggests KV fragmentation -> falling back to slower kernel. Need to check KV allocation alignment and eviction behavior.

sam: Agreed. Hypothesis: packing combined with variable-length KV pages causes misaligned allocations and extra copies. Try forcing KV prealloc aligned to 256B and observe kernel selector churn.

mike: I ran an experiment swapping the control knob: cap by max_batch_items (count) instead of payload. L4 throughput up ~7%, A10 throughput down ~6%. Looks like packing granularity favors L4 when we cap by items.

tara: Can we try a queue policy tweak too? e.g., head-priority for small requests to keep latency predictable, instead of strictly FIFO by arrival.

sam: Plan: run two sweeps in parallel: (1) payload-budget with KV_prealloc=256, (2) item-cap with head-priority queue. I'll kick off the jobs and post summaries.

perf-bot: job 1717004400 started: sweep-run-1 - payload-budget + KV_prealloc

sam: First pass highlights posted. Short summary: A10 sweetspot ~56k, T4 ~44k, L4 ~64k, A100 ~128k when KV_prealloc=256, H100 stable at 160k. Kernel_switch_count on A100 dropped to ~140 after prealloc. Full traces in S3.

leila: Nice. Please upload flamegraphs. Also note: our kernel selector rule currently flips to chunked-attn when kernel_switches > 150 — that explains the earlier throughput cliff on A100. We might tune that threshold or add a hysteresis window.

sam: Uploaded flamegraphs and traces: s3://perf/redwood/sweeps/1717004321/ (contains per-device flamegraphs + kernel metrics).

mike: Proposed runtime defaults based on sweep: set max_tokens_per_batch = {A10:56000, T4:44000, L4:64000, A100:128000, H100:160000}, KV_prealloc=256 for payloads > 64k, and add head-priority queue flag for latency-sensitive routes.

tara: +1 to defaults. Add canary rollout and monitor these metrics: p95, tokens/sec, kernel_switches, KV_eviction_rate, and OOM_count.

sam: I'll open a rollout ticket and checklist. Steps: canary on dedicated pool (20%), 6h window, alert on kernel_switches increase >20% or OOM.

perf-bot: ticket 1717004701 created: rollout-max-payload-defaults (canary)

sam: Thanks everyone. Will follow up with a short postmortem if any regressions show up. :thumbsup:
